Stan sources installed alongside executables: remaining sections use R wrappers load model sample posterior one call.
code: list_models() #>  [1] "bernoulli"               "CovMod_count"            #>  [3] "CovMod_dichotomous"      "MaltielBEM_count"        #>  [5] "MaltielBEM_dichotomous"  "MaltielBEM_trichotomous" #>  [7] "MaltielRDM_count"        "MaltielRDM_dichotomous"  #>  [9] "ZhengBEM_count"          "ZhengBEM_count2"         #> [11] "ZhengBEM_dichotomous"    "ZhengBEM_trichotomous"   #> [13] "ZhengGP_count"           "ZhengGP_dichotomous" mod <- get_model("ZhengBEM_count") class(mod) #> [1] "CmdStanModel" "R6" basename(mod$exe_file()) #> [1] "ZhengBEM_count" stan_file <- system.file("bin", "stan", "ZhengBEM_count.stan", package = "stansum") cat(readLines(stan_file), sep = "\n") #> data { #>   int N; #>   int K; #>   array[N, K] int y; #> } #>  #> parameters { #>   vector[N] alpha; #>   vector[K] beta; #>   vector<lower = 0 , upper = 1>[K] inv_omega; #>   real mu_beta; #>   real<lower=0> sigma_beta; #>   real<lower=0> sigma_alpha; #> } #>  #> model { #>   alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha); #>   beta ~ normal(mu_beta, sigma_beta); #>   for (k in 1:K) { #>     real omega_k_m1; #>     omega_k_m1 = inv(inv(inv_omega[k]) - 1); #>     for (i in 1:N) { #>       if (y[i,k] >= 0) { #>         real xi_i_k; #>         xi_i_k = omega_k_m1 * exp(alpha[i] + beta[k]); #>         y[i,k] ~ neg_binomial(xi_i_k, omega_k_m1); #>       } #>     } #>   } #> }

title: Getting Started with 'stansum'
text: examples use artificial dataset Fake_maltiel_RD shipped package. simulated Random Degree model Maltiel et al. (2015) 1000 respondents three subpopulations sizes 100000, 200000 300000 population 3 million. See ?Fake details. keep computations cheap use first 50 respondents . models expect ARD matrix respondents rows subpopulations columns: models accept dichotomous (respondent know anyone subpopulation: 0/1) trichotomous (knows nobody / one person / two : 0/1/2) responses instead counts (Baum Marsden 2023). derive counts: Maltiel et al (2015) models additionally need m – vector subpopulation sizes fractions population size – L – per-respondent lower bound degree. count models parametrize degree L + d_raw d_raw > 0, L must least largest number people respondent reported knowing subpopulation:
code: data("Fake_maltiel_RD", package = "stansum") head(Fake_maltiel_RD) #>   p1 p2 p3 #> 1  1  3  3 #> 2  1  1  5 #> 3  2  0  0 #> 4  2  2  1 #> 5  0  2  1 #> 6  0  3  1 y <- data.matrix(Fake_maltiel_RD)[1:50, ] N <- nrow(y) K <- ncol(y) y01 <- 1L * (y > 0) y012 <- pmin(y, 2) m <- c(1, 2, 3) * 1e5 / 3e6 L <- apply(y, 1, max)
